findings.title: Deployment images are selected by mutable tags
findings.what: All three deployable Compose definitions select a mutable image tag (latest or 2-alpine). A later registry retag can change the deployed executable without a repository change or review, defeating release provenance and creating a supply-chain exposure.
findings.fix: Replace each image reference with the approved immutable image digest, optionally retaining a human-readable version tag before @sha256.
findings.acceptance: `docker compose config` for each supported deployment shows every production image reference containing `@sha256:`; deployment of the same checkout resolves the same image digest on repeated runs.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read of the cited baseline lines confirmed the exact mutable references: ghcr.io/shpwrck/claude-history-dashboard:latest, ghcr.io/shpwrck/claude-history-dashboard-spa:latest, and caddy:2-alpine.

findings.title: Update transitive dependencies for body-parser and brace-expansion advisories
findings.what: The pinned baseline still resolves body-parser 2.2.2 and brace-expansion 5.0.6. A fresh npm audit reports the previously tracked body-parser denial-of-service advisory and both high-severity brace-expansion denial-of-service advisories, so #2865 remains current.
findings.fix: Trace both transitive paths and update the narrowest safe direct dependencies or lockfile resolutions to fixed versions.
findings.acceptance: npm audit no longer reports GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6, GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp, or GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg, and npm run validate remains green.
findings.verifyNote: Re-ran npm audit --json against the immutable baseline on 2026-07-26 and re-read the exact body-parser 2.2.2 and brace-expansion 5.0.6 lock entries.

findings.title: Resolve newly reported Hono, fast-uri, and PostCSS advisories
findings.what: A fresh npm audit at the pinned baseline reports five vulnerable dependency entries not covered by #2865: @hono/node-server and Hono through the bundled MCP SDK toolchain, fast-uri through production Ajv, and build-time PostCSS. The advisories cover path traversal, request-data confusion/disclosure and XSS, URI host confusion, and source-map path traversal; their exact shipped/build reachability has not yet been dispositioned.
findings.fix: Upgrade the narrowest direct dependencies and regenerate the lockfile; for any advisory that cannot be upgraded, prove and document why its vulnerable code path is unreachable in the shipped server, SPA, plugin payload, and build pipeline.
findings.acceptance: npm audit no longer reports GHSA-frvp-7c67-39w9, GHSA-xgm2-5f3f-mvvc, GHSA-hvrm-45r6-mjfj, GHSA-w62v-xxxg-mg59, GHSA-v2hh-gcrm-f6hx, GHSA-4c8g-83qw-93j6, or GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849; npm run validate and the plugin payload tests pass.
findings.verifyNote: Re-ran npm audit --json against the immutable baseline on 2026-07-26 and re-read all five cited lock entries and their direct/transitive classifications.
